inclusion_criteria: 70 consecutive patients who underwent a bilateral sagittal ramus osteotomy of the mandible

patients who have undergone orthognathic surgery

Forty consecutive patients scheduled to undergo intraoral orthognathic surgery were chosen as subjects.
exclusion_criteria: a history of allergy to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, a compromised immune defense, and a history of having received antibiotic therapy within 14 days before the planned surgery

inclusion_criteria: All patients, male and female, aged 18–40 years, who underwent bimaxillary orthognathic surgery within the Discipline of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery from December 2008 to May 2010, were enrolled in this study.
exclusion_criteria: Patients were excluded from the study when any of the following criteria were present: history of any type of previous surgery to the head and neck area, including previous orthognathic surgery; patients who were having distraction osteogenesis as part of the orthognathic surgery; history of malignancy of the head and neck region, and/or history of radiation to the head and neck region; known hypersensitivity to amoxicillin, ampicillin or other  $\beta$ -lactam antibiotics; known history of lactose intolerance; patients who had used any antibiotics in the 14 days prior to the surgery; patients with compromised host defences (e.g. diabetes mellitus, autoimmune disease, end-stage renal disease, severe alcoholic cirrhosis and neutropenia); and patients who were receiving immunosuppressive drugs that interfere with host defences (e.g. cyclosporine, steroids and cancer chemotherapeutic agents).
